finding.location: Subsystem 9: CG and Inertia, printed pp. 42-43; Ref. 26 on printed p. 53

model_method.finding: NASA CR-166536 describes a CG/inertia subsystem and points to Lanham (1979), ASD-TR-79-5004, for the calculation procedure; the supplied audit reports that the actual procedure/equations are not reproduced in the reviewed text.
model_method.rigid_body_model: The report is described by the audit as using a six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body aircraft model for flight-path dynamics.
model_method.component_transform: A fixed-airframe plus moving pylon/nacelle/rotor component decomposition is a possible calculation structure, not a verified XV-15-specific equation or completed calculation in this dataset.
model_method.required_inputs: Component masses; component own-axis inertia tensors; component centres of mass; conversion spindle coordinates; aircraft CG coordinates; geometry/orientation transforms; and consistent mass/configuration definitions.

moments_of_inertia.baseline_caution: NASA CR-166536 reportedly states that XV-15 inertia values were out of date because airframe modifications and flight-test instrumentation weights and locations were not included in the calculated inertias. Treat the S2 endpoints as historical baseline values, not automatically as validated flight-test configuration inertias.

flight_test_identification_caution.location: NASA TM-89428; exact page/table not supplied in audit

moments_of_inertia.flight_test_identification_caution: The supplied audit reports that frequency-response identification found the baseline simulation underestimated pitch and yaw inertia because nose/tail test ballast was omitted from the simulation database. The reported sensitivity ratio and percentage comparisons require direct page-level verification before being used numerically.
moments_of_inertia.transformation_equation: No source-documented closed-form inertia tensor transformation as a function of nacelle angle was identified in the reviewed material. Do not use a sine-squared curve, endpoint interpolation, or invented intermediate values as verified aircraft data.
moments_of_inertia.status_summary: Endpoint values are retained as historical source-reported values; intermediate-angle values and a reproducible source-grounded calculation remain unresolved.
